title: Isolated worktrees are not usable working environments: stale base ref and a shadowing empty node_modules
description:
**Two provisioning defects found on the FIRST real use of worktree isolation (TASK-195), 2026-08-03.** Both agents spawned into worktrees hit them; one refused to work, the other misdiagnosed one of them and committed a wrong fix. Neither is a defect in `src/worktree-handback.js` — both are properties of how the worktree is created and provisioned, which is why four review rounds on that module could not have found them.

**Defect 1 — the worktree is branched from a stale ref.** Worktree isolation branches from `origin/<default-branch>` by default (the `worktree.baseRef: fresh` behaviour). This repo is worked local-first: at the time of the incident `origin/main` was at `bc585e3` (2026-07-29) while local `main` was at `d3c80c1` (2026-08-03) — **63 commits and 5 days behind.**

Consequence: an agent spawned for TASK-193 landed on a checkout that predated TASK-185, the very ticket TASK-193 follows up on. `tasks/TASK-193.json` did not exist there, and the `UNSAFE_REF_RE` guard the brief cited at `src/mcp-server.js:105` was absent — the file:line references resolved to unrelated code. That agent correctly refused to work and reported rather than improvising; the TASK-189 agent instead fast-forwarded itself to `main` (a zero-conflict catch-up, disclosed in its hand-off).

Candidate fix: set `worktree.baseRef` to `head` in `.claude/settings.json` so worktrees branch from local HEAD. Note the Orchestrator was blocked from making this edit by the settings-file guard, so it needs a human or an explicitly-authorised path.

**Defect 2 — the worktree's empty `node_modules` shadows module resolution, and silently changes build output.** The worktree contains an empty `node_modules` directory. Node's parent-directory resolution fallback still satisfies ordinary `import`s, so most things appear to work — which is what makes this dangerous. Two things do NOT work:

1. `tests/vitest-changed-algorithm-pin.spec.js` (the TASK-194 sensor) does a literal `readdirSync` on `node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks` and fails ENOENT. Reproduced by the TASK-189 agent by stashing all its own changes — byte-identical failure, so genuinely environmental.
2. **`npm run build:plugin` emits different bytes inside the worktree.** `dist-parity` therefore reports drift that does not exist on main. The TASK-189 agent reasonably concluded the committed bundles were pre-existing stale, and committed six "refreshed" bundles built in the broken environment. The Orchestrator later verified `dist-parity` was GREEN on main all along — all 8 bundles byte-matched a fresh build — so the diagnosis was wrong and the six bundles were wrong.

**Why this matters beyond the incident:** an environment that is *almost* correct is worse than one that is obviously broken. Imports resolving via fallback is exactly what let the agent believe it was in a working tree, and the failure surfaced as a plausible-looking "pre-existing drift" story rather than an error.

**Both defects are pure provisioning.** Fixing them is likely configuration and setup, not logic — but the fix must be verifiable, because the failure mode is silence.
acceptance_criteria: Defect 1 is fixed so a newly-created worktree is based on the current local HEAD, not a stale remote ref. Demonstrate by creating a worktree and asserting its merge-base equals local HEAD.
Defect 2 is fixed so that inside a worktree, npm run build:plugin produces bytes identical to a build in the primary checkout. Demonstrate by building in both and byte-comparing all 8 bundles.

tests/vitest-changed-algorithm-pin.spec.js passes inside a worktree, or is made explicitly and loudly skipped there with the reason stated — a silently-passing skip is not acceptable, per the Empty-result contract.
A sensor exists that would fail if either defect regressed, rather than relying on an agent noticing. State plainly if a sensor is impractical for one of them and why.
The worktree-isolation guidance in skills/orchestrator-routing/SKILL.md records the provisioning requirements and how to verify them, in both parity copies byte-identical.
npm run test:all is green from BOTH the primary checkout and a worktree; report both results separately.

comments.author: reviewer
comments.body:
**BLOCK — REQUEST-CHANGES.** FULL depth, range `f8bc84b..fad9e25`. **1 HIGH / 2 MEDIUM / 3 LOW.**

**Gate:** `test:since -- f8bc84b` 32 files / 341 passed, 1 failed ⬛ `npm test` 86/87 files, 1151 passed ⬛ named e2e **25/25 including dist-parity across all 8 bundles** ⬛ `test:all` 186/188 files, 2153 passed, 1 failed ⬛ `check:calibration` clean ⬛ SKILL parity sha1 `f032ea1f…` identical. **The single failure in every run is the sanctioned expected-red sensor, failing for exactly its stated reason and nothing else.**

## HIGH — `removeMergedWorktree` destroys the primary's real `node_modules` through the junction

`src/worktree-handback.js:442`. **Reproduced in a sandbox** (git 2.53.0.windows.2): synthetic repo, clean merged worktree, gitignored `node_modules` junction pointing at a populated external directory → **non-force** `git worktree remove` exits 0 and **recursively empties the junction's target, subdirectories included.**

This is strictly worse than the disclosed incident, which used `--force`. Every guard in `removeMergedWorktree` — merged-ness, branch match, dirty check — **passes on the ordinary happy path**, because the junction is gitignored and therefore invisible to `git status --porcelain`. So the module's own doc comment at `:44` describing it as the one safe-disposal path is now false: it silently deletes the primary's dependency tree for every provisioned worktree it disposes of.

The provision → work → merge → dispose lifecycle this ticket standardizes in SKILL.md is a loaded gun. The new "Provisioning requirements" section says nothing about removal ordering, and `tests/e2e/git-worktree-handback.spec.js` has **zero** junction coverage (grep: no `junction|symlink|node_modules` match).

**The correct pattern already exists in this diff** — `src/worktree-provision.js:147` removes a junction with `rmSync(recursive: false)`, and a probe confirmed the foreign target survives intact.

**Fix:** in `removeMergedWorktree`, `lstat` the worktree's `node_modules` before `git worktree remove`; if it is a symlink/junction, unlink it non-recursively first, or refuse with a typed error naming the unlink step. Add an e2e test disposing of a provisioned worktree and asserting the primary-side tree survives. Document removal ordering in the same SKILL.md section, both parity copies.

**This is a defect this ticket should have closed** — the interaction was known (the incident occurred during this ticket's own development) and the junction convention shipped with the hazard unaddressed.

## MEDIUM

1. **`src/worktree-provision.js:135-140` — `E_NODE_MODULES_NONEMPTY` fires in a realistic ordering, with live evidence in the tree right now.** `.claude/worktrees/agent-a83ac659b232c8f2d/node_modules` is a real directory containing only `.vite/` and `.vite-temp/` — a vitest run inside an unprovisioned worktree writes its cache into the empty shadow, making it non-empty. Provisioning then refuses and directs a human to investigate. So **any spawn where the agent runs a single test before the documented "FIRST action" step permanently defeats provisioning until a human intervenes** — and since the seam is manual-by-documentation, that ordering will recur. The conservative refusal is right for unknown content; the gap is that the *predictable* cache-only shape is neither recognized as safely replaceable nor named in the error. **Fix:** treat a directory whose entries are all known cache dirs (`.vite`, `.vite-temp`, `.cache`) as replace-equivalent, or at minimum name that case and its resolution in the error.
2. **Pre-hand-off checklist** not visible in my inputs — Orchestrator to confirm against the hand-off. The claims the diff can test (parity, dist freshness) I verified independently and they hold.

## LOW

1. `src/worktree-provision.js:124` — a path-is-a-file throws a raw `ENOTDIR` from `readdirSync` rather than a typed refusal. Loud and destroys nothing (probe confirmed the file survives), and it does carry `.code`, but the message names an fs internal rather than the provisioning decision.
2. `tests/e2e/worktree-node-modules-provisioning.spec.js` — the `relink` action has **no real-fs coverage**. The Windows-critical behaviour (`rmSync(recursive: false)` removes the link without deleting through it) is exercised only by manual probe. A future change flipping it to `recursive: true` would recreate the HIGH-1 deletion class **with no sensor**. Add relink + dangling-link cases asserting the foreign target survives.
3. No primary-side sensor pins `preserveSymlinks: true` — removing it changes zero primary bytes, so `dist-parity` stays green there; the regression manifests only inside a worktree. Acceptable given the documented verification step, but the pin is environmental rather than unconditional.

## Verified good

**`preserveSymlinks: true` changes nothing but embedded path comments — confirmed two independent ways.** (1) Empirically: `dist-parity` rebuilds all 8 bundles under the *new* config and byte-matches committed `dist/` built under the *old* one. (2) Structurally: the flag acts only where resolution traverses a symlink, and the primary has none — no `file:`/`link:`/`workspace:` deps, no `workspaces` field, npm lockfile, and **zero symlinks in `node_modules`**. In a worktree the only link points at the identical tree, so module identity is unchanged and only nominal path strings differ. (Future caveat, not a finding: a pnpm migration or `npm link` would interact, but fails loudly at build time rather than silently substituting a module.)

**Provisioning-seam claim holds.** `hooks/hooks.json` wires only SessionStart; no settings file wires hooks; grep finds no `worktree add` anywhere in `src/`, `bin/`, `scripts/`, `hooks/`, `context-monitor/`. No in-repo seam exists, and refusing to add a never-firing hook was correct — though the `.vite`-poisoned worktree shows the manual step is *already* being skipped in practice, making the compensating control demonstrably weak.

**Pin sensor fix is clean.** Glob-by-prefix survived (`startsWith('git.') && endsWith('.js')` over a `require.resolve`-located chunks dir), no hashed-filename regression, and the `.toBe(1)` still fails loudly naming the found set. `require.resolve` additionally makes it correct in an *unprovisioned* worktree via Node's ancestor walk.

**AC1/AC6 status:** not yet satisfiable by design — the actual fix is the human-owned settings edit. The diff ships the sensor (red) plus a git-mechanics demonstration. **The ticket must not close until `worktree.baseRef: "head"` lands and the sensor flips green.**

comments.body:
**APPROVE** — fix round `0cd42d7`, base `ffb1a53`, FULL depth. **0 HIGH / 3 MEDIUM / 1 LOW.** The blocking HIGH is resolved.

**Gate:** `test:since -- ffb1a53` 31 files / 348 passed ⬛ `npm test` 86/87 files, 1159 passed ⬛ named e2e 3 files / 31 passed including all-8-bundle dist-parity ⬛ `test:all` 186/188, 2168 passed ⬛ `check:calibration` clean ⬛ SKILL parity sha1 `3aaa7512…` identical. The single failure everywhere is the sanctioned expected-red sensor. Later commits (`7ff4a30`, `8153091`) touch none of this ticket's seven files, so current-tree testing exactly reflects `0cd42d7`.

## Does the destruction still occur? No — reproduced both directions in OS temp

- **Without the fix (raw git):** synthetic repo, clean merged worktree, gitignored junction → non-force `git worktree remove` exits 0 and **recursively empties the target** (entries: `[]`). The hazard is real and still live in git itself.
- **With the fix:** identical setup → no throw, worktree disposed, **primary `node_modules` fully intact including nested subdirectory content.**

**Attacks:** junction pointing *inside* the worktree → severed and disposed, correct. Dangling junction → severed cleanly, no throw. Plain file at `node_modules` → left alone. **Guard ordering verified empirically** — a dirty worktree with a provisioned junction refuses `E_WORKTREE_DIRTY` and the junction is **still present after the refusal**, so the sever runs only after all four TASK-195 guards pass, immediately before `runGitOrThrow`. The fix adds **zero git calls**, so the module invariant at `:83-89` is untouched. Nothing TASK-195 hardened was weakened.

## MEDIUM-1 — nested junctions still delete through: the guard closes the shape, not the class

`src/worktree-handback.js:489`. Reproduced: a **real** `node_modules` directory containing a junction (`node_modules/nested-link` → populated foreign dir) passes the guard untouched — it only `lstat`s the top-level path — and `git worktree remove` **recursively emptied the foreign target.** Same data-loss class, one level down.

The new doc claim at `:81` and `SKILL.md:405` ("deleting it along with the rest of the tree is correct") is an **overclaim** for this shape, since deletion is then not confined to the worktree.

Mitigating: no framework path creates it — `worktree-provision.js` makes only the top-level link, and this repo's `npm install` produces zero `node_modules` symlinks. Residual risk, not a regression of the demonstrated HIGH. **Fix:** after severing (or when `node_modules` is a real dir), `lstat` its immediate entries and refuse with a typed error if any symlink/junction remains — or at minimum correct the doc claim in both parity copies.

## MEDIUM-2 — the lstat wrapper fails OPEN on a data-loss path

`src/worktree-handback.js:484-488`. The bare `catch { nodeModulesLstat = null; }` swallows **every** error, not just `ENOENT`.

**Scenario:** a transient `EPERM`/`EBUSY` (AV scan, ACL contention) on `lstat` of a still-present junction → guard silently skipped → `git worktree remove` proceeds → **the original destruction recurs.**

This contradicts the module's own fail-closed philosophy — git failures throw `E_GIT_FAILED`, but here an fs failure is treated as "nothing to sever". **Fix:** treat only `e.code === 'ENOENT'` as null; refuse with a typed error on anything else. Trivial diff.

## MEDIUM-3 — pre-hand-off checklist not visible in my inputs

Orchestrator to confirm. Everything independently testable — parity, dist freshness, red-run reproducibility, shim absence from the commit — verified and holds.

## LOW — the `recursive: true` comment is empirically overstated on this platform

`:491-494`. Sandbox check: Node's `rmSync(recursive: true)` on a Windows junction unlinks the link and **the target survives**, so flipping the flag would neither reintroduce the HIGH nor fail the new tests here.

**This does not weaken the sensors** — they assert the correct end-state invariant (foreign target survives), the disposal sensor demonstrably fails when the sever step is *removed*, and **git, not `rmSync`, is the actual destruction vector.** Suggest softening the comment to match `worktree-provision.js`'s accurate "on some platforms" hedge.

## Charges answered

**Unlink-vs-refuse:** auto-unlink is right. Removing a link never touches its target; the sever runs only after every refusal guard passes; a refusal would force each caller to duplicate the identical `rmSync` with no added safety. The one residual — sever succeeds, then `git worktree remove` fails — leaves a link-less worktree, but that failure is loud and `provisionWorktreeNodeModules`'s `create-link` recovers it.

**Cache-dir allowance:** exact and safe. `entries.every(name => KNOWN_CACHE_DIR_NAMES.has(name))` against a closed set; one unknown entry alongside cache dirs refuses. Case-sensitive `Set.has` fails in the safe direction; `isSymlinkOrJunction` and `isEmptyDir` take precedence; the `isCacheOnlyDir = false` default preserves prior caller behaviour.

**Red-run honesty:** sound. Both destruction sensors had genuine prior-wrong-behaviour to revert to, independently reproduced. The four non-red-planted specs exercise new decision branches with no prior wrong behaviour, and the pure matrix covers them exhaustively — appropriate for `tests-after`.

**Environment hygiene:** no shim leaked; the commit touches exactly the seven expected files.

**Primary checkout health at finish:** 33 `.bin` entries, zero lockfile drift, `require.resolve('vitest')` resolves from the primary. Identical to the starting snapshot; nothing modified.

## What still blocks close

1. **The human settings edit** — `worktree.baseRef: "head"`, flipping the sensor green (AC1).
2. **AC6's second half** — after that, `npm run test:all` must run **from inside a provisioned worktree** and be reported separately. Only the primary-side green exists today.
3. Housekeeping, not an AC: the poisoned `.claude/worktrees/agent-a83ac659b232c8f2d` is still present. With the cache-only allowance landed, provisioning can now reclaim it, or it can be disposed via the now-safe `removeMergedWorktree`.

comments.author: orchestrator
comments.body:
**DEFERRAL RECORD — 3 review items rolled forward. Human decision, 2026-08-04, credit-constrained.**

The fix round `0cd42d7` was APPROVED (0 HIGH). The blocking data-loss HIGH is closed and was independently reproduced in BOTH directions (destruction confirmed live without the fix; primary `node_modules` intact with it). The three items below are the residue of that APPROVE. **None blocks the approval and none is shipped-code-crucial** — recorded here so the next session picks them up without re-deriving the analysis.

Deferred deliberately, not forgotten. Ticket stays `in_progress`.

---

## Why deferral is defensible (the exposure argument)

`removeMergedWorktree` is only reachable when disposing a worktree, and the standing safety constraint in this session's `next_action` forbids worktree-isolated spawns until this ticket closes. **The affected path is therefore not being exercised at all.** That is what makes these deferrable — not their severity in the abstract.

---

## ITEM 1 — MEDIUM-2, do this FIRST. `src/worktree-handback.js:484-488`

```js
try {
  nodeModulesLstat = lstatSync(worktreeNodeModules);
} catch {                       // <-- swallows EVERY error, not just ENOENT
  nodeModulesLstat = null;
}
```

A transient `EPERM`/`EBUSY` (AV scan, ACL contention) on a **still-present** junction is read as "nothing to sever" → the guard is skipped → `git worktree remove` proceeds → **the original destruction recurs.**

This is the SIXTH appearance of this repo's most persistent defect class — a failure read as a benign answer (the Empty-result contract in CLAUDE.md catalogues the first four; this is the same shape). It sits *inside the fix for a data-loss hazard*, in a module whose own invariant at `:83-89` forbids exactly this shape. It slipped past because that invariant was scoped to `git()` results and this reads an `fs` result.

**Fix:** treat only `e.code === 'ENOENT'` as absent; refuse with a typed error otherwise. ~5 lines.

**MUST have a spec driving the non-ENOENT path** — a comment does not close this. **This is cheaper than it looks:** `vi.mock('node:fs', async (importOriginal) => ...)` is an established pattern here with 10+ existing uses, and `tests/worktree-handback-probe.spec.js` ALREADY mocks (`node:child_process`) for this exact module. No DI refactor is needed — inject a throwing `lstatSync` there.

**Severity in context:** real defect, but low-probability, and if it fires the damage is recoverable (`npm ci`) and loud (next build/test fails immediately). It fired twice on 2026-08-03/04 and was caught both times.

## ITEM 2 — MEDIUM-1. `src/worktree-handback.js:489`

The guard only `lstat`s the **top-level** `node_modules`. A real `node_modules` directory containing a nested junction passes untouched, and `git worktree remove` recursively empties the foreign target (reviewer reproduced this).

**Residual risk, NOT a live regression — do not inflate it.** No framework path creates that shape: `worktree-provision.js` makes only the top-level link, and this repo's `npm install` produces zero `node_modules` symlinks.

**Fix — either is acceptable:**
- (a) after severing, `lstat` the immediate entries and refuse with a typed error if any symlink/junction remains; **or**
- (b) the cheap half: correct the overclaim at `src/worktree-handback.js:81` and `skills/orchestrator-routing/SKILL.md:405` — "deleting it along with the rest of the tree is correct" is **false** for that shape. Both parity copies of SKILL.md, byte-identical.

## ITEM 3 — LOW. `src/worktree-handback.js:491-494`

The comment "recursive: true here would be the exact bug this fix closes" is **empirically wrong on Windows**: `rmSync(recursive: true)` on a junction unlinks the link and the target SURVIVES. **git, not `rmSync`, is the destruction vector.**

Does NOT weaken the sensors — they assert the correct end-state invariant (foreign target survives) and the disposal sensor demonstrably fails when the sever step is removed. Soften the wording to match `worktree-provision.js`'s accurate "on some platforms" hedge.

---

## STILL BLOCKS CLOSE (unchanged by this deferral — both are human-owned)

1. **`.claude/settings.json` needs `{"worktree": {"baseRef": "head"}}`** (AC1). The Orchestrator is structurally blocked from this edit by the settings-file guard, and that guard is correct. Verified absent again on 2026-08-04: the file has no `worktree` key at all. The sensor `tests/worktree-baseref-setting.spec.js` is RED by design until this lands — that is the sanctioned expected-red failure appearing in every gate run, not a broken test.
2. **AC6's second half** — `npm run test:all` must run **from inside a provisioned worktree** and be reported separately. Only the primary-side green exists today.
3. Housekeeping, not an AC: the poisoned `.claude/worktrees/agent-a83ac659b232c8f2d` (contains only `.vite/` + `.vite-temp/`) is still on disk. With the cache-only allowance landed, `provisionWorktreeNodeModules` can now reclaim it, or it can be disposed via the now-safe `removeMergedWorktree`.

## SAFETY CONSTRAINT — still in force

**Do not spawn worktree-isolated agents until this ticket fully closes.** The junction hazard fired twice in one day, both times during work aimed at it, each time emptying the primary's `node_modules/.bin`.

## Release context

v0.20.0 is being cut with this ticket deliberately left `in_progress`. That is sound: `0cd42d7` is already committed on main, so the release ships the verified HIGH fix regardless. What remains outstanding is local environment config (`.claude/settings.json` is not shipped to consumers) and a verification step — **not shipped bytes.** These three items land in the next version.

comments.body:
**APPROVE** — hardening round, range `f3bfd32..09455c8`, FULL depth. **0 HIGH / 1 MEDIUM (informational) / 3 LOW.** The prior round's blocking HIGH is discharged.

**Gate (reviewer-run, independent):** `test:since -- f3bfd32` 3 files / 22 passed, no zero-selection marker ⬛ `npm test` 87 files / 1160 passed, 2 skipped ⬛ `test:all` **188 passed | 1 skipped (189 files), 2171 passed | 4 skipped (2175), 0 failed** — reproduces the developer's primary-side report to the digit ⬛ `check:calibration` clean ⬛ SKILL.md parity sha1 `5d25d86232b2714ff15958521286690b8f09438d` on both copies, verified by direct hash.

**There is no longer any sanctioned expected-red in this repo.** `tests/worktree-baseref-setting.spec.js` is green as of `09455c8`. The 4 skips are pre-existing documented manual manifestos, none new.

## The three deferred items

- **MEDIUM-2 (fail-open lstat) — FIXED.** Only `e.code === 'ENOENT'` now means absent; anything else throws typed `E_NODE_MODULES_LSTAT_FAILED`, matching the sibling `E_NODE_MODULES_UNLINK_FAILED` convention.
- **MEDIUM-1 (nested junction) — option (b), doc correction, accepted as defensible.** The deferral record authorized either option; recursive descent would have added untested logic for a shape no framework path creates. The prior overclaim is corrected in all three places, each now carrying an explicit RESIDUAL RISK block naming the nested shape. `find node_modules -maxdepth 2 -type l` returns nothing, independently corroborating the residual argument.
- **LOW (`recursive: true` comment) — FIXED**, softened to the accurate hedge. No assertion touched.

## Five HIGH classes — all cleared

**Vacuous sensor — cleared by construction.** `E_NODE_MODULES_LSTAT_FAILED` exists in exactly one place (`src/worktree-handback.js:519`); the mock throws only for the exact worktree `node_modules` path, `lstat`ed only at `:501`. The passing assertion is itself proof the injected EPERM reached the new branch. The counterfactual is closed: with the bare `catch` restored there is no third path — EPERM → null → sever skipped → git succeeds → `thrown === null` → `expected null not to be null`. The thin message is an artifact of assertion ordering, not a weak test; the real-fs assertions would fail too. `vi.mock` has not neutered anything — the factory spreads `...real` and wraps only `lstatSync`.

**Stale dist — cleared two ways.** `grep -rn "worktree-handback"` across `src/ bin/ scripts/ hooks/` returns only the file's own header — zero importers, so it is unreachable from any of the 8 esbuild entry points; and `grep -l "removeMergedWorktree" dist/*.cjs` finds it in no bundle. `dist-parity` green. The no-rebuild claim is correct.

**Parity drift, calibration laundering, unspecced path — cleared.** The diff's epistemic direction is *toward* honesty: a claim was weakened to match evidence.

## AC6 — discharged by live Orchestrator-run verification

The reviewer's tool scope has no `git worktree`/`node`, so AC6's second half was escalated rather than approved on trust. The Orchestrator ran it and the evidence was checked against independent physical traces:

- **Worktree-side `test:all`** (fresh worktree off `09455c8`, provisioned via the real `provisionWorktreeNodeModules`, `action: create-link`, worktree's own settings confirmed carrying `baseRef: head`): **188 passed | 1 skipped (189), 2171 passed | 4 skipped (2175), 0 failed**, 105.89s — digit-for-digit identical to the primary-side line.
- **Corroboration:** `.claude/worktrees/` and `.git/logs/refs/heads/` mtimes moved to 15:36; `node_modules/.vite-temp` moved to 15:34, matching the reported `Start at 15:34:10` exactly. Mutually consistent, and not producible by the earlier observed state.

**The disposal FAILED — and that is the strongest evidence in this ticket.** `removeMergedWorktree` threw `E_GIT_FAILED` (`git worktree remove` exit 255, "Permission denied" on the directory — a Windows handle held seconds after a 105s in-worktree vitest run). Git failed **after** the sever, on a directory it had already emptied. Had the sever not run, git would have recursed through the junction at that moment and emptied the primary's `node_modules` — the historical damage signature. Instead: `node_modules/.bin` **33 entries before and after**, `require.resolve('vitest')` unchanged, `npm test` green afterwards. **This is the first live, non-synthetic exercise of the fix, and it prevented real data loss under a real failure rather than a mocked one.**

Honest caveat recorded: the pasted vitest output cannot be cryptographically bound to the worktree cwd. Every independently checkable assertion is true, the physical traces are exactly those a `create-link` worktree run leaves, and a fabricated discharge does not invent a failure that complicates its own story.

## Findings carried forward (none blocking)

- **MEDIUM (informational) — tier-audit.** `tests-after` on a diff mutating a data-loss disposal path; the narrowed rubric reserves `tdd` for state mutation with real edge-risk. Flagged transparently, not blocked: the risk the rule proxies for did not materialize — the deferral record *mandated* a spec driving the non-ENOENT path, the developer delivered one, and the red-run evidence was independently confirmed genuine. The substantive `tdd` bar was met under a `tests-after` label.
- **LOW-1** `tests/e2e/worktree-handback-lstat-failopen.spec.js:50-56` — `afterEach` uses `mockClear()`, leaving test 1's throwing override installed; safe today (distinct tmp paths, exact `===`) but order-coupled. Suggest `try/finally` restoring `realLstat`.
- **LOW-2** test 2 is a non-regression / over-fix guard, not a second red-green sensor. Named so the file is not later credited with two.
- **LOW-3** `E_NODE_MODULES_LSTAT_FAILED` undocumented in SKILL.md alongside `E_NODE_MODULES_NONEMPTY` — pre-existing family inconsistency, not new drift.
- **NEW, non-blocking → follow-up ticket.** `git worktree remove` **partially completed**: registry deregistered and directory emptied, then the root unlink failed. The caller gets `E_GIT_FAILED` and cannot distinguish "nothing happened" from "mostly happened". That is this repo's signature Empty-result class — an outcome the caller must infer. **Explicitly do NOT add a retry**: retrying a destructive git op on "permission denied" would paper over the one signal saying a live process still holds the tree.

**Verdict: APPROVE.** Safe to close, and — on this evidence — safe to lift the standing "do not spawn worktree-isolated agents" constraint: the disposal path has now been exercised live against a real provisioned worktree and failed *safely*, in the one direction that matters.

comments.body:

## The disposal failure — recorded because it is the best evidence in this ticket

The live AC6 disposal **threw** `E_GIT_FAILED` (`git worktree remove` exit 255, Windows "Permission denied" on the directory, a handle held seconds after the 105s in-worktree test run). This was not papered over, and it is not a defect in the change.

Git failed **after** the junction sever, on a directory it had already emptied. Had the sever not run, git would have recursed through the junction at that instant and emptied the primary's `node_modules` — the exact historical damage signature that fired twice on 2026-08-03/04. Instead: `node_modules/.bin` **33 entries before and after**, `require.resolve('vitest')` unchanged, `npm test` green afterwards. This is the **first live, non-synthetic exercise of the fix**, and it prevented real data loss under a real failure rather than a mocked one.

The reviewer's read, which I accept: a fabricated discharge does not invent a failure that complicates its own story.
